title: Lagaan Turns 25. Aamir Khan Is Taking It Back to the Big Screen — in Melbourne.
excerpt: The Academy Award-nominated epic gets a special IFFM anniversary screening on July 9, with Khan himself in attendance. Then he's heading to London.
body:
Twenty-five years ago, a three-and-a-half-hour Hindi film about dusty cricketers taking on the British Empire did something no one expected: it made the entire world care about *lagaan*.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=rZPbpymefuE

Now, Aamir Khan is flying to Melbourne to celebrate the moment that changed Indian cinema's relationship with the rest of the planet. On July 9, the Indian Film Festival of Melbourne (IFFM) will host a special 25th-anniversary screening of *Lagaan: Once Upon a Time in India* at the iconic ACMI cinema — with Khan in the audience.

The screening serves as the official curtain-raiser for IFFM's 17th edition, which runs August 13–23. But let's be honest: this isn't just a festival warm-up act. This is a pilgrimage.

The Film That Almost Didn't Happen

Directed by Ashutosh Gowariker and scored by A.R. Rahman, *Lagaan* was a bet nobody in the industry wanted to take. A period sports drama set in 1893, in Hindi, running 224 minutes, about farmers who've never played cricket challenging the British to a match to escape crippling land taxes. On paper, it sounded like a gorgeous way to lose money.

> "Rahman, *Lagaan* was a bet nobody in the industry wanted to take."**

Instead, it became one of only three Indian films ever nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film — a distinction it still holds alongside *Mother India* (1957) and *Salaam Bombay!* (1988). The nomination alone made it a cultural touchstone. The film's worldwide gross made it a commercial phenomenon. And Rahman's soundtrack — from *Mitwa* to *Ghanan Ghanan* — hasn't aged a day.

Why Melbourne, and Why Now

![Aamir Khan — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/65/Aamir_Khan_at_the_success_bash_of_Secret_Superstar.jpg)

The IFFM isn't just any film festival. It's the largest celebration of Indian cinema outside India, backed by the Government of Victoria. Over the years, it's hosted Shah Rukh Khan, Amitabh Bachchan, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, Ram Charan, Vicky Kaushal, and filmmakers like Rajkumar Hirani and Zoya Akhtar. But a *Lagaan* anniversary screening with Aamir Khan in person is an event with a different weight entirely.

For the Indian diaspora in Australia — one of the fastest-growing communities in the country — this is personal. *Lagaan* wasn't just a movie; it was the film their parents watched and rewound, the film that got played at community gatherings, the one they grew up quoting. Seeing it on a proper screen at ACMI, with the man who produced and starred in it sitting a few rows away, is the kind of experience streaming can never replicate.

> "There is no better way to begin our 17th edition than by celebrating 25 years of *Lagaan*. The film is a milestone in Indian cinema and continues to inspire generations of filmmakers and audiences around the world." — Mitu Bhowmick Lange, IFFM Festival Director

London Is Next

Melbourne isn't the only stop on Khan's anniversary circuit. He's also scheduled to appear at the London Indian Film Festival in July to mark the same milestone with British audiences — a fitting choice, given that the film's antagonists were, well, British.

The global tour underlines something Khan has always understood better than most Bollywood stars: the diaspora isn't a secondary market. It's home crowd, away.

What This Means for Diaspora Viewers

If you're in Melbourne, tickets for the July 9 screening at ACMI are available through the IFFM website. The full festival lineup drops on July 14, with the main festival running August 13–23.

For those in London, details on the LIFF screening are expected shortly.

And for everyone else watching from their living rooms in New Jersey, Toronto, and Dubai — *Lagaan* is streaming on Netflix in most territories. It's 224 minutes. Clear your evening. It's still worth every one of them.
